title: kv-cache: introduce memory rebalancer and spillover-aware eviction policy
author: Priya Singh
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncoordinated paging/spillover are causing elevated OOMs and tail latency on large-context workloads. This PR implements a memory rebalancer and a spillover-aware eviction policy to reduce fragmentation, prioritize compact/large contiguous allocations, and coordinate paging to disk to avoid cascading OOMs under pressure.

What this changes: introduced a background MemoryRebalancer that periodically scans GPU KV allocations and performs lightweight compaction and cooperative defragmentation; added a SpilloverEvictionPolicy which: 1) prefers evicting cold entries that free contiguous ranges, 2) delays eager paging when a spillover is likely to succeed, and 3) coordinates with the IO scheduler to smooth spike-driven disk flushes. Updated scheduler hooks so continuous batching can signal hot prefixes that should be pinned and exempted from aggressive eviction.

Files touched: runtime/kv_cache/{manager,rebalancer,eviction}.rs, runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs, runtime/io/spillover_queue.rs, tests/kv_cache/{unit,integration}_rebalancer.rs, benchmarks/kv_cache_rebalancer.toml, docs/observability/kv-cache.md.

Backward compatibility & rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime.enable_kv_rebalancer (default off for 2 weeks). Gradual canary rollout across Dedicated pools with telemetry monitoring for eviction rate, fragmentation ratio, paging spikes, and OOM counts. Rollback path included (toggle flag, revert ephemeral rebalancer state).

Testing: unit tests for eviction heuristics and compaction correctness; integration tests validate no regressed latency for short-context flows; stress tests under synthetic multi-model workloads to reproduce prior OOM pattern. Benchmarks attached: see benchmark_summary field.

Implementation notes: rebalancer runs with bounded CPU/GPU budget and uses non-blocking migration for KV slices. Eviction policy exposes scoring hooks so future ML-driven prioritization can be swapped in. The design is conservative to avoid impacting tail latency for low-memory workloads.

Related: ENG-4891 (kv fragmentation tracking), ENG-5020 (spillover stability), SUP-231 (support ticket tracking customer incident), PRs: prev experiments in pr-50730 and pr-51840 informed heuristics.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and doc updated

- [x] Canary rollout plan
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert rules

Notes: we observed transient CI flakiness on integration stress test; added a deterministic seed and extended timeouts. The rebalancer defaults to disabled in hosted for first 48 hours post-merge.

benchmark_summary: Microbenchmarks (8xA100 canary): fragmentation ratio reduced by 38% on mixed length workloads; OOM events in stress test reduced from 13 -> 1 over 1h run; 95th pct token latency improved by ~12% for large-context (32k) sequences; throughput maintained (+/-2%) for steady-state. IO spillover smoothing reduced peak disk writes by 45% and lowered GC-like pauses. See benchmarks/kv_cache_rebalancer.toml for raw data.
release_notes: Introduces a Memory Rebalancer and spillover-aware eviction policy for the KV cache. Improves OOM resilience and reduces fragmentation for large-context workloads; feature-flagged and rolled out via canary. Observability dashboards and alerts added. Default remains off for hosted for 48h post-merge.
